mainTopic: Agents for a גט: when the husband can retract, whether 'הולך' is like 'זכי', who can serve as a receiving or delivering agent, and an agent who changes the wife's words
overview: The משנה separates two kinds of agents for a גט. If the husband sends someone with the גט, he can change his mind until it reaches his wife. If the wife appointed someone to receive it for her, she is divorced as soon as her agent gets it, so the husband can no longer take it back, unless he openly refuses and says 'only bring it to her.' רבן שמעון בן גמליאל adds that 'take my גט for me' also makes a receiving agent. The גמרא tries three times to prove from the משנה that the husband's plain 'הולך' (deliver), said to the wife's receiving agent, counts like 'זכי' (acquire), and it pushes off each proof. Next it asks whether a man can be a receiving agent and a woman a delivering agent. It proves that a man can receive, since a father receives a גט for his young daughter. רב מרי and רב אשי prove from another משנה that a woman can deliver. Finally, רב rules on a case where the wife said 'bring,' the agent told the husband 'receive,' and the husband said 'as she said.' רב says she is not divorced even when the גט reaches her. The גמרא infers that the husband relied on the agent's words, and רב אשי begins to challenge that inference; his explanation continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The husband's own agent can be cancelled
steps.stepSummary: If the husband tells someone 'receive this גט for my wife' or 'deliver this גט to my wife,' he can still take it back.
steps.simpleTranslation: A man who says, 'Receive this bill of divorce for my wife,' or 'Deliver this bill of divorce to my wife,' may change his mind if he wants to.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה opens with the first case: the husband himself appoints the messenger.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This messenger works for the husband. The divorce only happens when the גט actually reaches the wife. Until then the husband can cancel, even if he used the word 'receive.'

keyTerms.meaning: Receive (here, said by the husband to his messenger)
Bring / deliver
Bill of divorce
To go back on it, to retract

steps.confusionAlert: Even though the husband said 'הִתְקַבֵּל' (receive), this is still the husband's messenger. The wife did not appoint him, so the word 'receive' does not finish the divorce here.

phrases.english: One who says: "Receive this bill of divorce for my wife,"
or: "Deliver this bill of divorce to my wife,"
if he wants to retract, he may retract.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: A messenger sent by the husband, whether told 'receive' or 'deliver,' can be cancelled until the גט reaches the wife.

steps.title: The wife's receiving agent cannot be undone
steps.stepSummary: If the wife appointed an agent to receive her גט, the husband cannot take it back once he hands it to that agent.
steps.simpleTranslation: A woman who said, 'Receive my bill of divorce for me': if the husband wants to take it back, he cannot.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the opposite case: here the wife appoints the agent to receive the גט for her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Her agent stands in her place. When he gets the גט, it is as if she got it herself, so she is divorced at that moment. There is nothing left for the husband to cancel.

keyTerms.meaning: An agent appointed by the wife to receive the גט for her
My bill of divorce

phrases.english: A woman who said: "Receive my bill of divorce for me,"
if he wants to retract, he may not retract.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Contrasts the wife's agent with the husband's agent from step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Once the wife's receiving agent gets the גט, the divorce is complete and the husband cannot retract.
steps.whatToRemember: Who appointed the agent is what matters. If the husband appointed him, the husband can cancel. If the wife appointed him to receive, the divorce takes effect as soon as her agent gets the גט.

steps.title: The husband can refuse to use her agent as a receiver
steps.stepSummary: If the husband tells the wife's agent 'I don't want you to receive it for her; just bring it to her,' he can still take it back.
steps.simpleTranslation: So if the husband tells her agent, 'I don't want you to receive it for her. Instead, bring it and give it to her,' he may change his mind until it reaches her.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה builds on step 2 ('לְפִיכָךְ', therefore). It shows that the husband can turn the wife's agent into his own delivery messenger.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The husband does not have to agree that the divorce happens at her agent. By refusing out loud, he makes the man his own messenger. Then step 1 applies, and he can cancel until the גט reaches her.

keyTerms.meaning: Therefore
I do not want
Bring it and give it to her

steps.whyThisMatters: The husband adds 'I do not want you to receive it' and does not just say 'bring it.' The גמרא later builds proofs on this detail (steps 9 and 14).

phrases.english: Therefore, if the husband said to him:
phrases.notes: 'Him' is the agent the wife appointed to receive her גט.

phrases.english: "I do not want you to receive it for her,
rather, bring it and give it to her,"
if he wants to retract, he may retract.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the rules of steps 1 and 2 to a case where the husband refuses the wife's appointment.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: By openly refusing to let her agent receive, the husband makes him a delivery messenger, and he can retract until the גט reaches her.

steps.title: 'Take my גט for me' also makes a receiving agent
steps.stepSummary: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says that a woman who says 'take my גט for me' has also appointed a receiving agent, so the husband cannot take it back.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: even a woman who says, 'Take my bill of divorce for me,' has made him a receiver, so if the husband wants to take it back, he cannot.
steps.whatsHappening: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל adds that a different wording from the wife also works as appointing a receiving agent.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is about wording. 'טוֹל' (take) could sound like she only wants the agent to carry the גט to her. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל holds that it means the same as 'receive,' so the divorce takes effect when her agent gets it.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא of the משנה
Take
Even

phrases.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
Even a woman who says: "Take my bill of divorce for me,"
if he wants to retract, he may not retract.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר: אַף הָאוֹמֶרֶת: ״טוֹל לִי גִּיטִּי״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the rule of step 2 to another wording.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'Take my גט for me' also appoints a receiving agent, so the husband cannot retract.

steps.title: Inference from the משנה: 'deliver' counts like 'acquire'
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בריה דרב אויא infers from the משנה that if the wife did appoint a receiving agent, the husband's plain 'הולך' does not let him retract. So 'הולך' is like 'זכי.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא בריה דרב אויא said to רב אשי: The reason the husband can take it back is that she did not make him her receiving agent. But if she did make him her receiving agent, then even when the husband says 'deliver,' he cannot take it back. Learn from this: 'deliver' is like 'acquire'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins. רב אחא reads a hidden implication out of the משנה and proposes a rule about the word 'הולך.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The husband can retract only because the wife never appointed a receiving agent. So if she had appointed one, his saying 'הולך' would not stop the divorce from taking effect at her agent. That means plain 'הולך' counts like 'זכי' (take possession for her).

keyTerms.meaning: The reason
She made him / appointed him
But (if the opposite were true)
Learn from this
Acquire / take possession (for her)
Is like, is the same as

steps.confusionAlert: רב אחא is not saying that every 'הולך' works like 'זכי.' He means only the case where the wife already appointed this man as her receiving agent.

phrases.aramaic: גְּמָ׳ אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אַוְיָא לְרַב אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: GEMARA: Rav Aḥa, son of Rav Avya, said to Rav Ashi:

phrases.aramaic: טַעְמָא דְּלָא שַׁוֵּיתֵיהּ אִיהִי שָׁלִיחַ לְִקַבָּלָה,
phrases.english: The reason is that she did not appoint him as an agent for receipt;
but if she did appoint him as an agent for receipt,
if he wants to retract, he may not retract.
Learn from this: "deliver" is like "acquire"!

steps.triggerLanguage: טַעְמָא דְּלָא שַׁוֵּיתֵיהּ אִיהִי שָׁלִיחַ לְִקַבָּלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws an implied rule out of the opening case of the משנה.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that the husband's plain 'הולך,' said to the wife's receiving agent, counts like 'זכי.'
steps.raayaSupportSource: What the first clause of the משנה implies: the husband can retract only because she did not appoint a receiving agent.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the question of how the husband's words relate to the agent's role. It decides the exact moment the divorce takes effect.

steps.title: Rejecting the proof: the משנה is teaching something else
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects רב אחא בריה דרב אויא's proof. It says 'הולך' may not be like 'זכי.' The משנה's case of 'התקבל גט לאשתי' was needed for a different reason: someone might think the גט fails, because the husband cannot appoint a receiving agent. The משנה teaches that his words mean 'receive and deliver.'
steps.simpleTranslation: No. I can tell you that 'deliver' is not like 'acquire.' The משנה needed to teach the case of 'Receive this גט for my wife' for its own reason. You might have thought that a husband cannot appoint an agent to receive, so even when the גט reaches her, it is not a valid גט. The משנה teaches us that he really meant 'receive it and deliver it.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes off the proof from Step 5. It explains that the משנה's case of 'receive a גט for my wife' is not about the wife's agent at all, so nothing can be learned from it about 'הולך.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אחא בריה דרב אויא learned his rule from what the משנה left unsaid. The גמרא answers that the משנה's case of 'התקבל' (receive) has its own new point. A husband is not able to appoint a receiving agent, so you might think his 'receive' words mean nothing and the גט fails even after it reaches her. The משנה teaches that we read his words as 'receive and deliver,' which makes the agent a delivery agent, so the גט works once she gets it.

keyTerms.meaning: Actually, I could tell you (the opening words of a rejection)
He needed to teach it (there is a reason the case was taught)
You might have thought (the mistaken idea the text comes to correct)
Able to appoint an agent
It teaches us (the new point)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two kinds of agents. A husband can only appoint a delivery agent (שליח להולכה). Only the wife can appoint a receiving agent (שליח לקבלה). So when the husband says 'receive,' the גמרא reads it as 'receive and deliver.'

phrases.english: No; actually I could tell you:
"Deliver" is not like "acquire,"
phrases.notes: So if the wife appointed a receiving agent and the husband told him 'deliver,' the husband could still take it back.

phrases.english: and the case of "Receive a גט for my wife" is what he needed to teach,
because you might have thought to say,
since a husband is not able to appoint
an agent for receiving,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל גַּב דִּמְטָא גִּיטָּא לִידֵהּ –
phrases.english: even though the גט reached her hand,
it should not be a valid גט;
so it teaches us
that he is really saying "receive and deliver."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the inference made in Step 5 by giving a different reason why the משנה taught its case.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof only. The rule itself ('הולך is like זכי') is left open, not disproved.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed the משנה's 'התקבל' case was about the wife's agent. It can instead be about a husband appointing an agent on his own, and it teaches that the גט is still valid.

steps.title: A second proof from the woman who said 'receive my גט for me'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings another proof that 'הולך' is like 'זכי.' The משנה rules that when a woman said 'receive my גט for me,' the husband cannot take it back. It does not say whether the husband used words of receiving or of delivering, so it seems both are the same.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in the משנה: a woman who said, 'Receive my גט for me,' if the husband wants to take it back, he cannot take it back. Doesn't that mean it makes no difference whether he spoke about receiving or about delivering?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries again to prove that 'הולך' is like 'זכי,' this time from the משנה's ruling about a woman who appointed a receiving agent.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says only that the husband cannot retract. It does not say which words he used when he handed over the גט. The proof argues that because the משנה makes no distinction, the rule should hold whether he said 'receive' or 'deliver.' If so, 'הולך' works just like 'זכי.'

keyTerms.meaning: We learned (in a משנה)
What, isn't it that... (opens a proof by suggesting a reading)
It makes no difference
Delivering (bringing the גט to her)

phrases.english: We learned: a woman who said:
phrases.notes: This is the same משנה ruling we saw back in Step 2.

phrases.english: "Receive my גט for me,"
if he wants to take it back, he cannot take it back.
What, isn't it that it makes no difference whether he used words of receiving
or words of delivering?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first proof was rejected, the גמרא offers a new proof for the same idea.
steps.raayaObject: That 'הולך' is like 'זכי' when the wife has appointed a receiving agent.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה: a woman who said 'receive my גט for me,' the husband cannot retract. It makes no distinction about which words the husband used.

steps.title: Rejecting the second proof: the ruling may only be about 'receive'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the second proof. The משנה's ruling that the husband cannot retract may apply only when he used words of receiving. If he said 'deliver,' he might still be able to retract.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it is talking about when he used words of receiving.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes off the second proof by limiting the משנה's ruling to a husband who said 'receive.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof depended on the משנה not making a distinction. The גמרא answers that the משנה could be talking only about the case where the husband said 'receive.' So nothing is proven about 'deliver,' and the question of whether 'הולך' is like 'זכי' stays open.

keyTerms.meaning: Receiving (the agent takes the גט on her behalf)

steps.whatToRemember: Both proofs that 'הולך' is like 'זכי' have been rejected. Neither one disproves the idea; they just show that the משנה does not force it. The question is still open at this point.

phrases.english: No, it is talking about receiving.
phrases.notes: He means the husband said 'receive this גט for her.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in Step 7.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the second proof only. The question itself is left unresolved.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed the משנה covers both kinds of wording. It may cover only the case where the husband said 'receive.'

steps.title: A third proof that 'deliver' is like 'acquire'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a third proof from the משנה. The husband can retract only when he clearly cancels the wife's agent by saying 'I don't want you to receive.' This suggests that plain 'הולך' alone is like 'זכי'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: 'Therefore, if the husband said to him: I do not want you to receive it for her; rather, deliver it and give it to her, then if he wants to retract, he may retract.' The reason is that he said 'I do not want.' But if he did not say 'I do not want,' he may not retract. Learn from this that 'deliver' is like 'acquire'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries again to prove that 'הולך' works like 'זכי', this time from the next line of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה lets the husband retract only because he said 'אי אפשי' and so took away the agent's role as the wife's receiver. That implies that if he had said only 'deliver' to her receiving agent, the agent would still receive for her and the husband could not retract. So 'הולך' would be as strong as 'זכי'.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear. This introduces a proof from a source.
Therefore. It continues the case in the משנה.
I do not want. The husband openly refuses the wife's agent.
The reason. The גמרא is about to make an inference from the reason.
But. It brings in the opposite case that the גמרא infers.

phrases.english: Come and hear: Therefore,
if the husband said to him:
"I do not want you to receive it for her;
rather, deliver it and give it to her,"
if he wants to retract, he may retract.
The reason is that he said "I do not want";
but if he did not say "I do not want,"
phrases.notes: In other words, he only said 'deliver it' to the wife's receiving agent.

phrases.english: if he wants to retract, he may not retract;
learn from it that "deliver" is like "acquire"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the second proof was rejected in step 8, the גמרא brings a third proof for the same idea.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's 'לפיכך' clause: the husband can retract only because he said 'אי אפשי'

steps.title: Maybe he said 'here you are'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. The משנה's unstated case might be one where the husband said 'הילך' ('here, it's yours'), which clearly means giving the גט to the wife.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps it is a case where he said "here you are."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes away the third proof. The inferred case may be one where the husband said 'הילך', not 'הולך'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof depended on the husband saying 'deliver'. If the case we infer is really 'הילך', which means 'here, it is hers', then of course he cannot retract. So we still have no proof about plain 'הולך'.

keyTerms.meaning: Perhaps. This opens a rejection.
Here you are. It is a clear word of giving and acquiring.

steps.confusionAlert: 'הֵילָךְ' (here, take it) and 'הוֹלֵךְ' (deliver) look and sound alike, but they mean different things. That difference is the whole point of this rejection.

phrases.english: Perhaps it is where he said "here you are."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 9.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the inference from the 'לפיכך' clause
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It assumed the husband said 'הולך', but the case may be 'הילך', which is clearly an act of giving.

steps.title: Can a man be a receiving agent, or a woman a delivering agent?
steps.stepSummary: A new question. A man can obviously be a delivering agent and a woman can obviously be a receiving agent. What about the reverse?
steps.simpleTranslation: It is obvious that a man can be an agent for delivery, since a husband delivers his wife's גט. And a woman can be an agent for receipt, since a woman receives her גט from her husband's hand. But a man for receipt, and a woman for delivery, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic: who may serve as which kind of agent for a גט.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The easy cases follow a simple rule: an agent can do what the person he stands in for can do. A husband delivers, so a man can deliver, and a wife receives, so a woman can receive. The question is whether an agent may do a job that his or her own gender never does in a divorce.

keyTerms.meaning: It is obvious.
An agent who delivers the גט for the husband.
An agent who receives the גט for the wife.
What is the law? This opens a question.

steps.whyThisMatters: It asks whether an agent's ability is tied to what the person he represents can do, or whether any agent can do any part of the process.

phrases.english: It is obvious that a man can be an agent for delivery,
since a husband delivers his wife's גט;
and a woman can be an agent for receipt,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁכֵּן אִשָּׁה מְקַבֶּלֶת גִּיטָּהּ מִיַּד בַּעְלָהּ.
phrases.english: since a woman receives her גט from her husband's hand.
A man for receipt, and a woman for delivery, what is the law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the 'הולך'/'זכי' discussion and opens a new question about who can be an agent.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a man may be a receiving agent and a woman a delivering agent for a גט.

steps.title: A proof from the משנה that one agent can do both
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that the משנה speaks of the same agent in both halves: the husband's delivering agent in the first half and the wife's receiving agent in the second. If so, an agent who is fit for receiving is also fit for delivering.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: one who says, 'Receive this גט for my wife,' or 'Deliver this גט to my wife,' may retract if he wants. A woman who said, 'Receive my גט for me': if the husband wants to retract, he may not. Is it not talking about one agent? Then learn from it that whoever is fit to receive is fit to deliver.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to answer the new question with a proof from the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof suggests reading the משנה as picturing one agent who can be sent by the husband to deliver and can also be appointed by the wife to receive. If the same person fits both roles, then a man can receive and a woman can deliver.

keyTerms.meaning: Receive. These are the words for appointing a receiving agent.
Is it not so? This introduces a suggested reading.
One agent.
Valid or fit.

phrases.english: Come and hear: one who says:
"Receive this גט for my wife,"
or "Deliver this גט to my wife,"
if he wants to retract, he may retract.
A woman who said: "Receive my גט for me":
if he wants to retract, he may not retract.
What, is it not about one and the same agent?

phrases.aramaic: וּשְׁמַע מִינַּהּ כָּשֵׁר לְקַבָּלָה כָּשֵׁר לְהוֹלָכָה?
phrases.english: And learn from it that one fit for receipt is fit for delivery?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to answer the question asked in step 11.
steps.raayaObject: That a man may receive and a woman may deliver
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's two halves read as speaking of one agent

steps.title: No, the משנה speaks of two different agents
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. The משנה may be describing two separate agents, a man who delivers and a woman who receives, so nothing is proven.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it is talking about two agents.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes away the proof. The two halves of the משנה may involve two different people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof worked only if one agent filled both roles. If the husband's agent and the wife's agent are different people, each one is doing the normal job. So this reading proves nothing, and the גמרא brings other proofs in steps 14-18.

keyTerms.meaning: Two agents.

steps.whatToRemember: This proof fails because the משנה can be read as speaking of two separate agents. Steps 14-18 go on to settle the question with other proofs.

phrases.english: No, it is about two agents.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 12.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the 'one agent' reading of the משנה
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It assumed a single agent, but the משנה may mean two agents, each doing his or her normal role.

steps.title: Another proof: the husband turns the receiving agent into a delivering agent
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings another proof from the משנה. The husband takes the same agent who was sent to receive and tells him to deliver instead. So one agent can do both jobs.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: 'Therefore, if the husband said to him, "I don't want you to receive it for her; rather, take it and give it to her," then if he wants to change his mind, he can.' Here it is one single agent. So learn from this: someone fit to receive is also fit to deliver.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries again to answer the question from step 11. It points to the משנה, where one person is first sent to receive the גט and is then made into a delivering agent.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 13 the proof failed because the two halves of the משנה might describe two different agents. Here the case itself is about one agent: the wife's receiving agent, whom the husband turns into his own delivering agent. That seems to show that one agent can fill both roles.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear, the גמרא is bringing a proof
Therefore
I don't want
Whoever is fit to receive is also fit to deliver

phrases.english: Come and hear:
Therefore, if the husband said to him:
phrases.notes: 'Him' is the agent the wife sent to receive her גט.

phrases.english: "I don't want you to receive it for her,
rather, take it and give it to her,"
if he wants to retract, he may retract.
And here, it is one agent,

phrases.aramaic: וּשְׁמַע מִינַּהּ כָּשֵׁר לְקַבָּלָה כָּשֵׁר לְהוֹלָכָה!
phrases.english: so learn from it: fit for receiving is fit for delivering!

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: לְפִיכָךְ, אִם אָמַר לוֹ הַבַּעַל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 13 rejected the 'two agents' reading, this proof uses a case that clearly has only one agent.
steps.raayaObject: Whether an agent fit for receiving is also fit for delivering
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's case where the husband turns the wife's receiving agent into a delivering agent

steps.title: Partly accepted: a man can be a receiving agent
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא accepts part of the proof. It shows that a man can be a receiving agent. That makes sense, since a father receives a גט for his young daughter.
steps.simpleTranslation: Resolve from it that a man can be an agent for receiving, since a father receives a גט for his young daughter.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא says the last proof settles one half of the question: a man can be a receiving agent.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The agent in the משנה could be a man, so the proof only covers a man doing both jobs. A man receiving is not surprising, because the הלכה already lets a father receive a גט for his daughter who is a קטנה. This proof does not show that a woman can deliver; steps 17 and 18 prove that.

keyTerms.meaning: Resolve from it
A father receives a גט on behalf of his daughter
A girl who is a minor

phrases.english: Resolve from it
that a man can be an agent for receiving,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁכֵּן אָב מְקַבֵּל גֵּט לְבִתּוֹ קְטַנָּה;
phrases.english: since a father receives a גט for his minor daughter;

steps.triggerLanguage: פְּשׁוֹט מִינַּהּ אִישׁ הָוֵי שָׁלִיחַ לְקַבָּלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the proof from step 14 so that it covers only a man as a receiving agent.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A man can serve as a receiving agent for a גט.

steps.title: Still open: can a woman be a delivering agent?
steps.stepSummary: The part that is still unresolved is whether a woman can be a delivering agent.
steps.simpleTranslation: A woman as a delivering agent: ask about it. What is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא names the half of the question that the last proof did not answer. This sets up the next two proofs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof in step 14 only worked for a man. So the question narrows to the other side: can a woman carry a גט from the husband to the wife?

keyTerms.meaning: Ask about it; this part is still in doubt
Delivering the גט from the husband to the wife

phrases.english: A woman for delivering:
ask about it, what is the law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Picks out the part of step 11's question that step 15 left unanswered.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Can a woman serve as the husband's delivering agent for a גט?

steps.title: רב מרי: women who may not report a death may still bring a גט
steps.stepSummary: רב מרי cites a משנה. Even women who are not believed to say a woman's husband died are believed when they bring her גט. Bringing a גט is delivering, so a woman can be a delivering agent.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב מרי said: Come and hear: 'Even the women who are not believed to say that her husband died are believed to bring her גט.' And there, it is delivering.
steps.whatsHappening: רב מרי answers the question about a woman delivering. He uses a משנה that lets women bring a גט to the wife.
steps.deeperAnalysis: That משנה is about women bringing a גט from the husband to the wife, which is exactly delivering. Since those women count as valid bringers of the גט, a woman can be a delivering agent.

keyTerms.meaning: Are believed
To bring her גט to her
And there, in that case

phrases.english: Rav Mari said: Come and hear:
Even the women who are not believed
phrases.notes: This is a משנה earlier in this מסכת (23b). These are women suspected of wanting to harm her.

phrases.english: to say her husband died,
are believed to bring her גט,
and there, it is delivering.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב מָרִי, תָּא שְׁמַע: אַף הַנָּשִׁים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question raised in step 16.
steps.raayaObject: A woman can be a delivering agent
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה (23b) that says women are believed to bring a גט

steps.title: רב אשי: the end of that משנה proves it too
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי says the end of the same משנה also proves it. A woman may bring her own גט if she declares 'it was written and signed before me.' That case was already explained as delivering, so the matter is settled.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: You can also learn it from the end of that משנה. It teaches: 'The woman herself may bring her own גט, as long as she says, "It was written before me and it was signed before me."' And we explained that case as delivering. Learn from it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי adds a second proof from the end of the same משנה, and the גמרא closes by accepting it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In that case the woman carries her own גט and acts as the husband's delivering agent, the way the גמרא explained it earlier. If a woman can deliver even her own גט, a woman can clearly be a delivering agent. The words שמע מינה mark the question as settled.

keyTerms.meaning: From the end of the משנה too
It was written before me and signed before me, the declaration made when a גט is brought from abroad
And we already explained it as
Learn from it; the point is proven

steps.whatToRemember: A man can be a receiving agent, and a woman can be a delivering agent. The משנה of 'women who bring a גט' proves the second point.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
From the end of the משנה too, learn it,
as the end of the משנה teaches:
The woman herself may bring her own גט,
as long as she must say:
"It was written before me and signed before me";
and we explained it as delivering;
phrases.notes: The גמרא worked this out earlier in the מסכת: she carries the גט as the husband's delivering agent.

phrases.english: Learn from it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: מִסֵּיפָא נָמֵי שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second proof to רב מרי's and closes the question.
steps.raayaObject: A woman can be a delivering agent
steps.raayaSupportSource: The end of the same משנה: a woman may bring her own גט, explained as delivering
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A woman can serve as a delivering agent.

steps.title: New case: the wife said 'bring,' the agent said 'receive,' the husband said 'as she said'
steps.stepSummary: A new אמוראic case is introduced. The wife told the agent 'bring me my גט.' The agent told the husband 'your wife said receive my גט for me.' The husband gave it and said 'here, as she said.'
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: She said, 'Bring me my גט.' The agent said, 'Your wife said: receive my גט for me.' And the husband said, 'Here it is, as she said.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic, a case where the wording does not match. It is only describing the case here; the dispute about it comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The wife asked for a delivering agent ('bring'), but the agent told the husband he was a receiving agent ('receive'). The husband's words 'as she said' are unclear: do they follow what she really said, or what the agent reported? That changes when the divorce takes effect.

keyTerms.meaning: It was stated, introducing a statement or dispute of the אמוראים
Bring me my גט, wording for a delivering agent
Receive my גט for me, wording for a receiving agent
Here it is, as she said

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up 'bring' (הבא) and 'receive' (התקבל). With 'bring,' she is divorced only when the גט reaches her hand. With 'receive,' she is divorced as soon as the agent takes it.

phrases.english: It was stated:
"Bring me my גט,"
and "Your wife said: receive my גט for me,"
and he said: "Here it is, as she said";

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the question of who can be an agent was settled.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sets out the case of 'bring' and 'receive' wording that do not match, before the אמוראים argue about it.

steps.title: רב rules she is not divorced even when the גט reaches her
steps.stepSummary: רב rules that in the case of the agent who changed her words, the woman is not divorced, even after the גט actually reaches her hand.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said in the name of רבה בר אבוה, who said in the name of רב: Even if the גט reached her hand, she is not divorced.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives רב's ruling on the case from Step 19, where the agent misquoted the wife. He says she is not divorced at all, even once the גט gets to her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We might have thought that once the גט physically reaches her, she should be divorced, since she really did send the agent to bring it. רב says no, and the word 'even' (אפילו) shows that this is the surprising part. The agent's switch from 'bring' to 'receive' ruins the whole agency.

keyTerms.meaning: Even. It signals the surprising part of the ruling.
It reached her hand, meaning she physically has the גט.
Divorced.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: Rav Naḥman said that Rabba bar Avuh said that Rav said:
Even if the bill of divorce reached her hand,
she is not divorced.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the ruling on the case set up in Step 19.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the agent turns 'bring me my גט' into 'receive my גט for me,' the woman is not divorced, even when the גט reaches her hand.

steps.title: Inference: the husband relied on the agent's words
steps.stepSummary: From רב's ruling, the גמרא infers that the husband relied on the agent's words ('receive'), not on the wife's real words ('bring').
steps.simpleTranslation: Learn from this that the husband relies on the agent's words. For if he relied on her words, then at least once the גט reaches her hand, she should be divorced!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws a lesson from רב's ruling. It explains why she is not divorced: the husband handed over the גט based on what the agent told him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The husband said 'here, as she said,' and we need to know which version he meant. If he meant her real words ('bring'), the agent would be a delivering agent, and the divorce would work once the גט reached her. Since רב says it does not work, the husband must have meant the agent's version ('receive'). She never appointed him as a receiving agent, so the agency fails completely.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from this. It introduces an inference.
Statement, words.
He relies on.
At least.

steps.confusionAlert: 'His words' here means the agent's words, not the husband's. The question is whether the husband trusted the agent's version or the wife's real request.

phrases.english: Learn from this
that he relies on his statement,
phrases.notes: 'His statement' is the agent's version: 'receive my גט for me.'

phrases.english: for if he relied on her statement,
then from when the bill of divorce reaches her hand,
at least let her be divorced!

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ אַדִּיבּוּרָא דִידֵיהּ קָא סָמֵיךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a principle out of רב's ruling in Step 20.
steps.raayaObject: That when a husband gives a גט to an agent, he relies on the agent's own claim about what kind of agent he is.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב's ruling that she is not divorced even when the גט reaches her hand.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the question of whose words decide what kind of agent the messenger is. That question is exactly what רב אשי is about to challenge.

steps.title: רב אשי objects to the inference
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי says the inference does not follow. His full explanation comes on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: How can you say that?!
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי begins to reject the lesson the גמרא just drew. This line only sets up his argument, and his explanation continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אשי is not yet arguing with רב's ruling itself. He is challenging the claim that the ruling proves the husband relied on the agent's words. He will show that there is another way to explain why she is not divorced.

keyTerms.meaning: How can these be compared? A common phrase for rejecting a proof.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
How can these be compared?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a rejection of the inference made in Step 21.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The inference about whose words the husband relied on. רב's ruling itself is not being rejected.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Not yet stated. רב אשי's reasoning continues on the next amud.
